citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
There is one dog "Blue" (M, Dachshund, #9936) 6yrs old, that has moderate to severe buildup of brown/black
tarter/calcified material that appears to encapsulate the back two molars on the upper left side cheek teeth of the mouth.
The upper back molar on the right side of the cheek teeth and last lower molar on the right side of the cheek teeth has a
moderate buildup of brown/black tarter/calcified material covering the surface of the two teeth. The gums appear red and
swollen with a foul odor from the mouth.
There are two dogs that have a moderate buildup of brown tarter/calcified material covering the surface area on the
majority of their upper and lower cheek teeth on both sides, at times connecting the teeth together. There are signs of
moderate recession of the gums that appear red and swollen in some areas with the calcified material pushing up into the
gums, with accompanied foul odor. The dogs are "Charlie" (M, Cavalier, #7524) 2yrs old, liver/white and Blue/gray; and
"KoKo" (F, Dachshund, #7101) 7yrs old, Choc/tan. The licensee advised that he fell behind on the cleaning of the dogs
teeth and has not taken them to the attending veterinarian for dental care.
The moderate to severe buildup of tarter/calcified material on teeth can be a source of bacteria and infection in the
regulated animals, possibly causing serious health issues if not under a regular dental program with the attending
veterinarian. The lack of proper dental care can cause inflammation of the gums, gingivitis and possible tooth loss which
can cause unnecessary pain or discomfort to the regulated animal.
There is a dog "Cherry" (F, Corgi, #3932) 6yrs old, red sable, that has a circular wound (approx. 1/2in diameter) at the top
of her head at the base of her left ear. The area is raw and fleshy and pink and moist in appearance. The wound had not
been observed prior to the inspection. Both ears had a moderate buildup of white scaley material inside the ear surface
and at the tips of the ears. The dog was observed tilting her head to the left, holding her ears down and shaking her head
during the inspection and appeared to be in discomfort. Both eyes were runny. The licensee advised they thought the dog
had an allergy a month prior and treated her with verbal direction over the phone by the attending veterinarian. However,
when the ear condition did not resolve the licensee failed to take the dog to the veterinarian for proper diagnosis and
treatment.
The lack of proper and timely diagnosis and treatment of medical conditions by the attending veterinarian can cause
unnecessary pain and discomfort for the regulated animals. The delay in veterinary treatment can cause a curable
condition to become chronic or more serious if left undiagnosed or treated for extended periods of time. The visible signs
of a dog shaking or tilting their head, scratching their ears repeatedly and/or drooping ears that normally stand up can be
a sign that there is a health issue that needs to be addressed.
The licensee must use appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries.
To be corrected by: "Cherry" was seen by the attending veterinarian on September 3, 2026
for proper diagnosis and treatment. The attending veterinarian is working with the licensee on treating the dental issues.

There are six water bowls that have a moderate buildup of hair/dirt/debris in the top and/or bottom of the bowls. While
they do have water available, the bowls are not being cleaned often enough to provide clean potable water for the dogs.
The buildup of dirt/debris and hair in the water bowls could be a source of bacteria and other health issues due to
dehydration if the dogs do not drink the water as they should.
Water receptacles must be kept clean and sanitized in accordance with § 3.11(b).
To be corrected by: The bowls were cleaned by the end of the exit interview

There are six dogs that have long nails that are not being trimmed monthly, according to their written program of vet care.
Two examples are "Cherry" (F, Corgi, #3932) 6yrs old, red sable, and a poodle "Maddie" (F, #9142) 2yrs. old, white, with
nails that are approximately 1/2-3/4 inch overgrown from the quick. The licensee advised that he has gotten behind on his
monthly nail trims and has not gotten them done in a while.
Not following the minimum schedule/standards on the signed program of veterinary care in regards to the preventative
maintenance of nails/hair trims, eyes, skin and teeth; could result in possible health issues, disease, or injury and
discomfort to the regulated animals.
The licensee must follow their signed program of veterinary care as written by the attending veterinarian in regards to
preventative care and treatment to ensure healthy and unmatted hair coats, properly trimmed nails, and clean and healthy
eyes, ears, skin, and teeth.
To be corrected by: The nails were trimmed by delivery of the inspection report on September 4, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with licensee.
